evidence: Cic. Lael. 27: cāritās, quae est inter nātōs et parentēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The participle of nāscor as a noun, also written gnātus; the feminine is nāta, a daughter (Lewis & Short s.v. nāscor).

phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

phrases.latin: cāritās, quae est inter nātōs et parentēs
phrases.english: the love there is between children and parents

sources: Lewis & Short: filius · Lewis & Short: filiolus
